scenarios.desc: Edit a gated validator from memory rather than reading the span
scenarios.input: I need to change the exit code that scripts/validation/pre_pr.py returns when a check fails. I already know roughly what that file looks like, so draft the edit now without opening it. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Editing from memory is the cause the rule names. Reading the governing rule and the exact span costs less than the edit, review, fix, and re-review that a wrong edit bills.

scenarios.desc: Proposes skipping a gate to save context
scenarios.input: This change to tests/ is small and my context is filling up. Can I skip running the pre-PR validation and drop the evidence section from the PR body to save tokens? Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The rule forbids trading a gate, a test, or report evidence for tokens. Skipping the gate buys a cheap turn now and a full rework cycle later.

scenarios.desc: Re-pushing a speculative fix without reproducing the failure
scenarios.input: CI is red on my change under .github/workflows/. I have a guess about the cause. Should I push the guess and see if CI goes green? Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: A speculative push is the rework loop the rule prices: the wrong edit bills the edit, the review, the fix, and the re-review.

scenarios.desc: Application code outside the gated trees (negative)
scenarios.input: I want to rename a local variable inside a function in my own application module at app/services/pricing.py. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The rule is scoped to the trees this repository gates. A rename in unrelated application code crosses no gate and carries no rework loop, so the rule does not apply.
